stem: Why must a program written in a high-level language be translated?

options.content: The processor can execute only machine code
High-level programs cannot be stored in main memory
options.rationale: They can be stored; they simply cannot be executed directly.

options.content: High-level languages contain no instructions
options.rationale: They contain instructions in a form people can read.

options.content: The processor can read only text
options.rationale: The processor reads binary machine code.

explanation: Only machine code can be executed directly.

stem: Which translator produces a complete object code program from a high-level language program?

options.content: A compiler
An interpreter
options.rationale: An interpreter executes statements without saving a translated program.

options.content: A text editor
A linker
options.rationale: A linker joins object code files; it does not translate source code.

explanation: A compiler translates the whole program before it is run.

stem: What is an advantage of an interpreter during the development of a program?

options.content: The program runs faster than when it has been compiled
An error is reported at the statement where it occurs
The source code is hidden from the person using it
options.rationale: That is a benefit of delivering object code.

options.content: The whole program has to be free of errors before it can start

explanation: Interpreters allow quick trial and correction.

stem: Why does a software company usually deliver object code rather than source code to its customers?

options.content: Object code is always smaller than any other form of the program
options.rationale: Size is not the main reason.

options.content: Source code cannot be read by a computer under any conditions
options.rationale: The reason concerns privacy and a translator.

options.content: Customers need to be able to correct the errors themselves
options.rationale: Customers do not need to change the program.

options.content: It runs without a translator and the source stays private

explanation: Object code needs no translator and does not reveal how the program was written.
hints: What does the customer need in order to run object code?

stem: Why can byte code run on many different types of computer?

options.content: Byte code is machine code for every type of processor made
options.rationale: It is not machine code for any one processor.

options.content: Byte code does not need to be translated or interpreted at all
options.rationale: It is interpreted by the virtual machine.

options.content: The source code is recompiled again on every computer used
options.rationale: The byte code is not recompiled.

options.content: Each computer has a virtual machine to interpret the byte code

explanation: The virtual machine hides the differences between processors.
hints: Which program runs the byte code on each computer?

stem: Which IDE feature allows a programmer to stop a program at a chosen line so that the values of the variables can be examined?

options.content: Pretty-print
A breakpoint
Dynamic syntax checking
options.rationale: That underlines errors as they are typed.

options.content: Collapsing a code block

explanation: A breakpoint pauses execution at a line.

stem: What is the purpose of dynamic syntax checking in an IDE?

options.content: It runs the program one statement at a time under user control
It points out syntax errors as the code is typed
It converts the program to machine code
It sets the colour of the keywords

explanation: Errors are flagged before the program is run.

stem: A programmer has finished a program that a bank branch will run every day for years. Which translator is the better choice for the final version?

options.content: An interpreter, because it hides the source code from users
options.rationale: An interpreter needs the source code.

options.content: An assembler, because the program is in a high-level language
A compiler, because it translates once and runs faster
No translator, because the bank's processor reads text

explanation: A program run many times benefits from being translated once.
hints: How many times will the program be run?

stem: An interpreter produces a file of object code that can be run later without the interpreter.
explanation: False. An interpreter executes the statements directly. A compiler produces object code.

stem: A compiler reports the syntax errors in the program after it has tried to translate all of it.
explanation: True. Compilation fails if there are syntax errors, and the errors are reported.

stem: Match each IDE feature to what it does.

right.content: Shows the current values of variables
Lays out the code with indentation and colour
Suggests keywords and names as you type
Runs the program one statement at a time
Pauses the program at a chosen line

stem: Complete the sentences.

payload.template: An {{blank:a}} translates assembly language into machine code. A {{blank:b}} translates the whole of a high-level program before it runs. An {{blank:c}} translates and executes one statement at a time.

explanation: Assembler, compiler, interpreter.

stem: Compiling a program takes 20 s. The compiled program takes 0.5 s to run. Interpreting the same program takes 2.5 s each time it is run. What is the smallest number of runs for which compiling and then running is faster overall than interpreting?
explanation: At 10 runs the totals are equal (25 s); at 11 runs compiling is faster.
workedSolution:
1. Compiled: 20 + 0.5n. Interpreted: 2.5n.
2. Compiling is faster when 20 + 0.5n < 2.5n, so 2n > 20 and n > 10.
3. The smallest whole number is 11.
hints: Compiled total = compile time + runs × 0.5; interpreted total = runs × 2.5.

stem: Using the figures in the previous question, what is the total time in seconds to compile the program and run it 20 times?
workedSolution:
1. 20 runs × 0.5 s = 10 s.
2. Add the compile time: 20 + 10 = 30 s.
hints: Add the compile time to 20 runs of the compiled program.

stem:
This program is run:

```
Total ← 0
FOR N ← 1 TO 10
    IF MOD(N, 3) = 0 THEN
        Total ← Total + N
    ENDIF
NEXT N
OUTPUT Total
```

What is output?
explanation: Total is 18.
workedSolution:
1. The values of N from 1 to 10 divisible by 3 are 3, 6 and 9.
2. Total = 3 + 6 + 9 = 18.
hints: Trace the loop: which values of N are exactly divisible by 3?

stem: The program in the previous question is single stepped in an IDE. The variable report window is read after each loop pass. What does it show for `Total` when `N` is 7?
explanation: Total is 9 until N reaches 9.
workedSolution:
1. Total changes at N = 3 (to 3) and N = 6 (to 9).
2. At N = 7 it is still 9.
hints: Total changes only when N is divisible by 3.

stem: Name the IDE feature that runs a program one statement at a time.
explanation: Single stepping.

stem: Compare a compiler with an interpreter. [4]

points.description: A compiler translates the whole program before it is run; an interpreter translates and executes one statement at a time
A compiled program runs faster / an interpreted program is slower because each statement is translated every time it is run
A compiler produces object code that can be distributed without the source code; an interpreter needs the source code each time
An interpreter finds an error at the statement where it occurs, which suits testing; a compiler reports errors after translating the whole program

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: A compiler translates the whole program before it is run, while an interpreter translates and executes one statement at a time. A compiled program runs faster, whereas interpreted statements are translated each time they are run. A compiler produces object code that can be given to users without the source, but an interpreter needs the source each time. An interpreter stops at the statement with the error, which suits testing.

explanation: Four contrasting pairs.

stem: Some languages are partly compiled and partly interpreted. Explain how this works and one benefit. [3]

points.description: The source code is compiled to an intermediate code (byte code)
A virtual machine interprets the byte code on the user's computer
Benefit: the same byte code runs on any computer that has the virtual machine (portable)

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The source code is compiled to byte code, which a virtual machine then interprets on the user's computer. The same byte code can run on any computer that has the virtual machine, so it is portable.

explanation: Byte code, virtual machine, portability.
hints: Name the intermediate code and the program that runs it.

stem: A student is learning to program and changes her program many times a day. Explain why an interpreter and an IDE with single stepping are suitable. [4]

points.description: An interpreter runs the program straight away after each change, without a separate compile stage
It reports an error at the statement where it occurs, so errors can be found and corrected quickly
Single stepping runs one statement at a time
The variable report window shows how values change, which helps to find logic errors

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: An interpreter runs the program straight after each change and reports an error at the statement where it occurs, so it can be corrected quickly. Single stepping runs one statement at a time and the variable report window shows how the values change, which helps her find logic errors.

explanation: Quick feedback and insight into the program.
hints: Think about errors found while testing.

stem:
A programmer in Kariba uses an IDE to test this program, written in pseudocode (and also in Python):

```
Total ← 0
FOR N ← 1 TO 10
    IF MOD(N, 3) = 0 THEN
        Total ← Total + N
    ENDIF
NEXT N
OUTPUT Total
```

She sets a breakpoint on the `OUTPUT` line and single steps through the loop first. The report window shows these values of `N` and `Total` after each pass:

| N | Total |
|:-:|:-:|
| 0 | 0 |
| 1 | 0 |
| 2 | 0 |
| 3 | 3 |
| 4 | 3 |
| 5 | 3 |
| 6 | 9 |

(only the first six passes are shown).

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: State the value of `Total` after the pass where `N` is 6.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: State the value displayed by the program when it ends.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Which IDE feature allows her to see the values of `N` and `Total` while the program is paused?

options.content: Pretty-print
Dynamic syntax checking
options.rationale: That finds errors as they are typed.

options.content: A variable report window
Collapsing code blocks

parts.explanation: The report window shows the values.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: Describe the purpose of a breakpoint and of single stepping, and say how the two are used together.

points.description: A breakpoint stops the program at a chosen line
Single stepping runs one statement at a time
Set a breakpoint at the section of interest, run to it, then single step through it while watching the variables

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: A breakpoint stops the program at a chosen line, and single stepping runs one statement at a time. They are used together by running to a breakpoint just before the part of interest and then stepping through it while watching the variables.

parts.explanation: Each feature, then the way they combine.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Which translator should the company use to make the version it sells?

options.content: Interpreter
options.rationale: An interpreter would need the source code.

options.content: Assembler
options.rationale: The program is not in assembly language.

options.content: Compiler
Text editor

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Give two reasons for your choice.

points.description: The object code runs faster because it is already translated
The source code is not given to the customers / is protected

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The object code runs faster because it is already translated, and the company does not have to give the customers its source code.

points.description: A change can be run immediately without compiling the whole program
